name: extended
description: Everything in the base profile plus the modern WinUI3 controls with no WinForms counterpart: dialogs, info bars, command/menu bars, pickers, shapes and the richer button family. Exists both as the next step up from base and as the exercise of profile composition -- it adds to base rather than restating it.

packages.comment: Microsoft.UI.Xaml.winmd only *references* Microsoft.UI.Windowing, .Composition and .Dispatching; without their metadata Window.appWindow, .compositor and .dispatcherQueue are dropped as unresolved. They arrive as bare shells, since a type the walk finds on its own generates no members.

Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.DispatcherQueue.comment: The way work reaches the UI thread, and the way the event loop is asked to stop. Reached by the walk through Window.dispatcherQueue, so a root only because a discovered type generates no members.
Whole surface: what CreateTimer hands back is worth nothing without Interval, IsRepeating, Start/Stop and Tick.

Microsoft.UI.Windowing.AppWindow.comment: The way a window's position and size are controlled at all: Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Window exposes none of it and hands out an AppWindow instead. The walk already reaches this type through Window.appWindow, but a type it finds on its own generates no members, so it has to be a root to be worth anything.

Microsoft.UI.Windowing.AppWindowTitleBar.comment: The window's own title bar, which a XAML window shares with its AppWindow: whether the client area runs up into it, how tall the caption buttons the system draws over that area are, and how much room they take on either side. Window.ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar is a wrapper over the property of the same name here; PreferredHeightOption and the insets have no wrapper at all, so an application reaches them through Window.appWindow. The button colours are left out: they are IReference<Color>, and core::nullable<Color> has no representation yet -- every bit pattern of a Color is a colour, so there is no sentinel to compress the empty state into.

Microsoft.UI.Windowing.OverlappedPresent.comment: The configuration of an ordinary window, and the only supported place a minimum or maximum size can be said. Create is a static member -- the class has no activatable constructor -- and is reached through the cached statics proxy.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.UIElement.comment: Two members on top of what base asks for, and they only work as a pair: Shadow names what is cast, Translation.Z is what lifts the caster off the page -- a shadow with no elevation is invisible.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.ThemeShadow.comment: The system shadow: blur and darkness are derived from Translation.Z, so a card says only how high it floats. Receivers is left out -- WinUI3 casts onto whatever lies beneath without being told, and the member would put Collection<UIElement> into the Media group, closing an include cycle with Microsoft.UI.Xaml.h that #pragma once resolves into truncated declarations.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.TitleBar.comment: The content of a title bar a window has taken over, laid out the way Windows lays it out: headers on either side, content between them, room kept for the caption buttons, a strip that always drags. What makes it more than a Grid is input: it cuts Passthrough regions for everything interactive inside it, so the buttons in a caption still get their clicks, and it dims itself while the window is inactive. It is handed to the window with setTitleBar; neither hiding the system caption nor drawing the caption buttons is its job.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.FontIcon.comment: An icon named by a code point in a font the application names itself, which is why it is here and not in the base profile: it is the way out to a font of one's own -- a brand's icon set, a private-use glyph -- at the price of naming that font and trusting the machine to have it. For the system icon set it is no longer needed at all: SymbolIcon takes wxl's FluentSymbol as well as WinRT's Symbol, so every glyph the icon font documents is named there, and the baseline profile alone suffices.

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.FlipView.comment: A page at a time, swiped or clicked through. Selection comes from Selector in the base profile, so what is left of its own is the direction it flips in; the type is listed here as much to give the nine FlipViewButton* brush keys of the theme dictionaries a control to belong to.
